probe.name: json-value-close-trajectory-rmsd
probe.rationale: Attempts analysis A with a wrong value: replaces the open-vs-closed reference RMSD with the final trajectory backbone RMSD (6.820321761026975), an unambiguously different quantity (difference ~0.0034, far above the 1e-6+1e-6*r tolerance). The JSON object still contains exactly the keys value/unit with unit "angstrom" and a finite non-negative number, and no other file is changed, so only the analysis_a scientific comparison can reject it.
probe.script:
import json, io

p = "open_closed_backbone_rmsd.json"
with io.open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    obj = json.load(f)
bound = 1e-6 + 1e-6 * abs(obj["value"])
with io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(json.dumps({"value": 6.820321761026975, "unit": "angstrom"}))
assert obj["unit"] == "angstrom"
assert abs(6.820321761026975 - obj["value"]) > bound

probe.name: backbone-core-vs-ca-core
probe.rationale: Attempts analysis B with a CORE selection error: the CORE-domain backbone RMSD column is replaced by the CORE alpha-carbon RMSD from analysis C (CA-only selection instead of the N,CA,C,O backbone). import csv

probe.rationale: Attempts analysis D with the wrong weighting scheme: every mass-weighted CA and domain RMSD row is replaced by the value of the similar residue-number-weighted variant (analysis E). probe.script:
import csv

pR = "resid_weighted_rmsd.csv"

    csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)

probe.name: time-ps-frame-index-offset
probe.rationale: Attempts the time_ps convention with an off-by-one frame indexing mistake: the per-frame time is written as the 0-based frame index (frame k -> k ps, first frame at t=0) instead of the accepted (frame + 1) ps or tool-reported convention. The saved times are shifted by about 1 ps (differences of ~1 >> the 1e-4 ps bound) while all RMSD columns, headers, row counts and frame indices are unchanged, so only the time_ps comparison fails.
probe.script:
import csv
files = ["backbone_domain_rmsd.csv", "ca_core_rmsd.csv", "mass_weighted_rmsd.csv", "resid_weighted_rmsd.csv"]
for p in files:
    with open(p, "r", newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    assert rows[0][0] == "frame" and rows[0][1] == "time_ps"
    assert len(rows) == 99
    for row in rows[1:]:
        frame = int(row[0])
        assert abs(float(row[1]) - (frame + 1)) < 1e-4
        row[1] = "%d" % frame
    with open(p, "w", newline="") as f:
        csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)

probe.name: ca-csv-float-string-style
probe.rationale: Representation control: the CSV field semantic values (frame index, time_ps, RMSD) are unchanged, only the saved numeric strings are re-serialized (formatted decimal and standard float repr, Python repr being the shortest exact round-trip encoding of the parsed value), which stays within the ordinary CSV float round-tripping covered by the 1e-6 atol and keeps every structural constraint satisfied.
